newsitem.title: NIGERIA: NIGERIA'S UBA SAYS REFORM HIT PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: NIGERIA'S UBA SAYS REFORM HIT PROFITS.

text.p: Internal reforms and deepening recession were behind a fall in full-year profits at Nigeria's UBA United Bank for Africa, one of the country's big three, bank officials said on Wednesday.
"We are trying to improve on computerisation and we have spent a lot of money on re-organisation," one senior official said.
UBA on Wednesday said after-tax profit in the period to the end of March 1997 was 919 million naira against 1,000 million naira a year earlier.
UBA paid significant compensation to hundreds of laid-off staff last year as it tried to slim down and become more efficient to do business in Nigeria's recession-hit economy, company sources said.
They said efforts, including the introduction of Saturday retail banking across the country as well as extending opening hours, were being intensified to win market share.
UBA shares fell 40 kobo to 12.50 naira on the news of lower profits. They said the downturn was contrary to their expectations.
